genes/FLAJ1/Fjoh_1066/Fjoh_1066-ai-revie.description: Fjoh_1066 encodes LolB1, a structurally divergent LolB-like lipoprotein in Flavobacterium johnsoniae UW101. Native deletion and complementation implicate it in delivery of a subset of lipoproteins to the outer membrane, including clients needed for gliding and type IX secretion. Its predicted LolB fold, lipoprotein signal and functional loop support an inferred outer-membrane insertion role. These studies establish cellular trafficking function rather than a purified-protein insertion reaction. Other paralogs and retained lipoprotein localization in strains lacking known LolA/LolB proteins show that LolB1 is neither universally essential nor the only delivery route.

This does not imply direct participation in gliding or T9 secretion, universal essentiality, or exclusive delivery of all lipoproteins.

genes/ECOLI/lolA/lolA-ai-review.yaml.description: LolA is the soluble periplasmic carrier that transfers mature outer-membrane lipoproteins between LolCDE in the inner membrane and LolB at the outer membrane of Escherichia coli. LolA then delivers cargo to LolB for membrane insertion. LolCDE normally excludes inner-membrane retention substrates at the extraction step. LolA is essential in ordinary E. coli backgrounds, although conditional bypass of LolA and LolB is possible when lipoprotein toxicity and envelope stress responses are altered.

LolD powers extracytoplasmic cargo extraction rather than transport of cargo through the inner-membrane bilayer.
